slides.title: The Simple Secret of LLMs 🤫
slides.content:
# The Autoregressive Objective

Despite their astonishing capabilities, modern Large Language Models (LLMs) like GPT-4, Claude, and LLaMA are trained on a deceptively simple objective:

$$\max_\theta \sum_{t} \log P_\theta(w_t \mid w_1, w_2, \dots, w_{t-1})$$

* **Next Token Prediction:** Given all words seen so far, calculate a probability distribution over the entire vocabulary (50,000+ tokens) for the next token.
* By scaling this objective across **trillions of tokens of human writing, code, mathematics, and science**, the model implicitly learns grammar, factual knowledge, coding logic, and reasoning patterns!

slides.title: Chinchilla Scaling Laws (Hoffmann et al., 2022) 📏
slides.content:
## Optimal Scaling
For compute-optimal model training, model parameters and training dataset size should be scaled in equal proportion:
* For every doubling of model parameters, the training token count should also double.
* Training smaller models on vastly more high-quality tokens produces faster, cheaper, and more accurate models at inference time!
